baseBranch: main (sjawhar/legion#1843 is based on main; the branch head 24cbcaad carries the forward merge of main@origin 5c956b07; the implementer starts on legion/LEGION-631@origin, which carries this handoff)
concerns: Every phase completion now reads GitHub (branch, contents, READY's checks): an outage or a rate limit holds completions as 502 until the worker completes again; nothing retries in the daemon
A handoff's shape error surfaces after the push (at completion), not at write time; the fix is a new commit and push
The CI-skip decision is the worker's: a wrong trailer stalls the issue (no verdict carried, or READY refused for want of checks) and never passes it

The skip recipe's `jj describe --config templates.commit_trailers=""` must keep the existing message and its Omp-Session trailer with skip-checks last; the implementer proves it on jj 0.45 in the smoke
Explicit thread ids: nothing stops a reviewer naming a thread it did not read; the skill forbids it

Image drift replaces a pod at the next relaunch of any of its roles, interrupting live roles in it once; a pod already running an older image at the pin is covered only by the runbook's drain-or-relaunch rule and the boot warning

`legion threads resolve` stays the one agent bash `legion` command (and the one reader of the bash grant mint) until the LEGION-656 thread question is answered; acceptance 4's grep excludes `threads` deliberately
#1842 (LEGION-632) also declares contract 16; whichever of it and #1843 merges second renumbers again
The skill-scenarios rig is hand-run, not CI-gated; it is rewritten and must be run once
designSummary: Round 2 for spec v4 keeps the delivered token-file design and adds the deletion set: no 'Legion never merges' line anywhere (prompts, skills, README, docs/site; the GitHub-issue rule stays); the pi-legion jj operation-log refusal mechanism (PaneRule and all) deleted, the rule kept as prompt text with `jj undo` added; `legion push` deleted in favour of a written procedure (ancestry revset, per-commit path listing, `jj describe --config templates.commit_trailers=""` appending `skip-checks: true` as the last line for plan/test/changes_requested-review handoffs only, keyword self-check, `jj bookmark set` + `jj git push`), the daemon's path classification unchanged; the `Accepted:` rule deleted by making `legion threads resolve` and POST /legion/v1/threads/resolve take explicit thread ids (reviewer-only; the implementer resolves with plain gh api graphql; the two App-login variables and legionAppLogins go); the whole `legion handoff` CLI group and the tool's handoff_write/handoff_read deleted — a worker writes .legion/<issue>/<phase>.json with `write`, commits, pushes, and the tool's handoff_complete posts {grantId, summary, verdict?, ready?} directly; the daemon reads the issue branch head from GitHub (/branches/legion/<KEY>), refuses a head not authored by the role's App, reads the file at that head (/contents) and checks its shape with handoff_schema.go moved to internal/handoff, runs READY's checks server-side, all before intake.ApplyFact; `legion state` for agents becomes read_record and the controller gets a `legion` tool with read_state and set_status; image drift logged at boot and added to relaunch's replace triggers, with the drain-or-relaunch runbook rule in docs/kubernetes.md and the PR body; contract 17's paragraph rewritten (number unchanged unless main takes 17 first).

findings.answer: Push before complete is a hard rule, written in the push procedure and every role's handoff paragraph; the daemon creates legion/<KEY> before any role starts (outbox.createBranch), so a 404 branch is 409 HANDOFF_BRANCH_MISSING; a head without the file is 409 HANDOFF_FILE_MISSING; a head already reported is HANDOFF_NOT_NEW; lib/workflow.sh's '(the commit need not be pushed)' comment is rewritten.
findings.finding: Reading the completion's commit as the branch head on GitHub makes a push mandatory for every completion; today the commit is read from the pane's jj and need not be pushed, and the branch need not exist.

findings.answer: LastHandoff stays confined to phase.FileBacked (engine.go:343-348); for retro, READY and the production check the head is recorded without a dedupe and TestHandoffCompleteRecordsRetroThenProductionCheckAtOneCommit stays green; the plan says so (item 5 step 5).
findings.finding: HANDOFF_NOT_NEW on head == LastHandoff would break retro then production check at one commit if extended past file-backed phases.

findings.answer: Every new step (repository, head, author, file+shape, READY) is a writeFailure placed after redeem/role checks/handoffPosition and before ApplyFact (:110); a transient GitHub failure is 502 GITHUB_READ_FAILED with no key recorded (item 5, lead paragraph).
findings.finding: The moved READY checks and the new GitHub reads must run before intake.ApplyFact or a refusal is recorded under the completion's event key and the retry is HANDOFF_ALREADY_RECORDED.

findings.answer: Options.Repository(project) from the daemon's config (as outbox.createBranch resolves it) and Options.GitHubAPI; endpoints GET /branches/legion/<KEY> (measured: slashed name works, answers sha and commit.author.email) and /contents/...?ref=<sha> (measured); codes NO_REPOSITORY 409, HANDOFF_BRANCH_MISSING 409, GITHUB_READ_FAILED 502 for everything else; no retry; the outage exposure is named as a risk.
findings.finding: Every completion now depends on GitHub and on project configuration for the repository and branch; failure modes, endpoints and repo resolution were unstated.

findings.answer: commit.commit.author.email equals appauth.AppRoleFor(role)'s lease Identity.Email (<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com; implementer and merger → implement App, the rest → review App), else 409 HANDOFF_AUTHOR_MISMATCH; a lease that cannot be minted is the existing GITHUB_TOKEN_FAILED 502 since the reads need it anyway.
findings.finding: The author check changes identity source: name, email or login, and the behaviour when the lease cannot be read.

findings.answer: The worker writes schemaVersion: 1, phase (required, equal to the word), issue (required, equal to the grant's issue), completed (RFC 3339, type-checked) plus the phase's fields; the daemon checks at completion; skills/legion-worker/SKILL.md:345-375, tester.md:9, planner.md:36-39, implementer.md are rewritten; a failed shape check is followed by a new commit and push (item 5, risks).
findings.finding: With handoff_write gone, the four fields the CLI stamped have no owner and the handoff-writing instructions are wrong.

findings.answer: Plain read of $LEGION_WORKSPACE/.legion/<issue>/<phase>.json; after retro's removal `jj file show -r 'latest(::@- & files(".legion/<KEY>"))-'`; the root architect reads a child's file from the issue branch with gh api contents or the shared clone; rootArchitectHandoffRefusal goes with the ops; the flat-path fallback is dropped since every tree on main writes the per-issue directory and the pin drains or relaunches pods.
findings.finding: Deleting handoff_read leaves the root architect and every predecessor read without a stated route; the legacy flat-path fallback disappears.

findings.answer: Acceptance 4b gives the exact commands: `./legion --help | grep -E '^\s*(gh|credential|push|handoff)\b'` empty and `rg -n -e 'legion (state|status|push|handoff|gh|credential)\b' packages/daemon/internal/prompts skills packages/pi-legion/src/tools.ts` empty — literal, so prompts and skills do not describe the operator CLI; prompts_test.go:43,97 are task 7's work.
findings.finding: Acceptance 4's grep and the `legion --help` line are not machine-decidable as written, and prompts_test.go:43 and :97 pin the deleted sentences.

findings.answer: Item 3's five-step procedure reproduces each: remove a stale trailer on a non-skipping push with the same describe, read the last line back, grep for the five keywords, list paths per commit over legion/<KEY>@origin..@- with `jj log --summary`, and the ancestry revset `legion/<KEY>@origin ~ ::@-` plus `jj bookmark set` without --allow-backwards and jj git push's own refusal; the describe re-emits the existing message read with -T description.
findings.finding: The plain-jj push rule drops five guards legion push enforced: stale trailer removal, the read-back assertion, bracket keywords, paths from commits not net diff, the remote-ancestry refusal.

findings.answer: The command and base (legion/<KEY>@origin) are given; the three files, existence at @-, and review.json's changes_requested verdict are spelled; the two wrong-trailer outcomes are stated (code path: no verdict carried; a fourth .legion/ file: verdict carried but READY refuses a head with no checks) — both stall, neither passes; truncation is unreachable for ≤3 paths.
findings.finding: The agent evaluates the skip allow-list by hand with no stated command, and the daemon's rule (any .legion/ path) is wider than the agent's three files.

findings.answer: Recorded as spec departure 1 with the evidence that no rule remains once the text check goes; new shapes (threads in the request; withheld dropped; refused kept), an already-resolved id answered as resolved so retries are idempotent, an id off the pull request refused before any write, and the reviewer's listing query are in item 4.
findings.finding: Explicit-id thread resolution is not 'as it works today, less the Accepted: rule': the request, the response and the reviewer's job change.

findings.answer: Only the env plumbing, appauth.LoginEnv, api.legionAppLogins (the threads route's sole caller) and reviewthreads' bot rule go; appLogins from mintAtBoot, reviewAppLogin and classify.ByReviewApp stay (item 4, fourth bullet).
findings.finding: Deleting the two APP_LOGIN variables must not delete appLogins, which the engine needs for acceptance 5.

findings.answer: lib/workflow.sh's bot_thread_resolved_on_acceptance and thread_accepted_unresolved are rewritten to author-only checks, the review-thread checkpoint resolves by id, README:306-309,848-849 are rewritten, and README:1648-1658 says the recorded commit is the branch head at the accepted completion (the tester's head is its red-tests commit, still its own App).
findings.finding: e2e helpers and the stage README encode the Accepted: rule and the 'commit carrying the handoff' semantics.

findings.answer: read_state calls client.state() with no grant (GET /legion/v1/state is open) and passes api.State through; set_status mints the controller grant via controllerSession.mintGrant ({sessionId, secret}); LegionToolSession for the controller carries kind and sessionId with tree/issue optional; the worker pane's mint path stays so stage 3's grant-mtime probe keeps working.
findings.finding: The controller tool: read_state needs no grant, and the tool's session shape for a controller is unspecified.

findings.answer: The boot warning lives in ReconcileOrphans's informer-store loop (sandbox.go:746-756), compares every container's image (role and init) to r.image; relaunch.go:85 gains imageDrift as a replace trigger with a new relaunch_test.go case; the controller's pod is in scope and its relaunch happens only when its process is being started anyway; a refusal at adopt is rejected as unsafe.
findings.finding: The image-drift mechanism as first stated did not fit the code: the known-claims loop reads no pod, relaunch_test.go names no image, and the controller pod is in the blast radius.

findings.answer: The paragraph (version.go:69-93) is rewritten, not extended; pi-legion CHANGELOG Unreleased and contracts/CHANGELOG.md:149 are corrected; the plugin's version is the release workflow's to bump (chore: release commits), not this PR's; renumber only if main takes 17 first.
findings.finding: Contract 17's paragraph becomes false in three places and the pi-legion CHANGELOG's Unreleased entry repeats the deleted facts; the plugin version question.

findings.answer: Request {grantId, summary, verdict?, ready?} (commit removed), response {note?: string}; legion-api.ts:407-412, legion-api.test.ts:52,170-173, fixture handoff-complete.json, state_golden_test.go:354, controller_test.go:372 named in item 5; inside unreleased 17.

findings.finding: Deleting the jj operation-log refusal leaves `jj undo` with no guidance anywhere; headless.md names only op restore, abandon, edit @-.

findings.answer: Item 1 lists every docs/site and README line; kubernetes.md:1812-1818 is deleted; the rollout rule is a new subsection after the v10.0.0 one; sixteen docs/solutions notes get a superseded line (task 12) and pane-lifetime-files' existing line is extended.

specDepartures.evidence: internal/reviewthreads/reviewthreads.go:106-141 chooses threads by isAcceptance(thread.NewestBody) alone; once the text check is deleted no rule remains for which threads close, and the identity-only reading (any newest reply by the opener, or by the reviewer on a bot's thread) would close a thread on a 'Still open:' reply — the distinction api/threads_test.go:138-186 is built on. Explicit ids need no comment rule and survive every answer to the LEGION-656 question.

outcome.scope: POST /legion/v1/threads/resolve's request gains `threads` and its response loses `withheld`; `legion threads resolve` is reviewer-only and takes ids; the implementer resolves threads with plain gh; LEGION_IMPLEMENT_APP_LOGIN and LEGION_REVIEW_APP_LOGIN are not set on tree launches.

specDepartures.plan: `legion threads resolve` and POST /legion/v1/threads/resolve take explicit thread node ids and read no comment: the reviewer lists threads with gh api graphql, replies, and names the ones to resolve; the daemon still accepts only the reviewer's grant and the issue's recorded pull request, refuses an id off that pull request, resolves as the implement App and logs each. The non-reviewer branch of the CLI and --gh go: the implementer, the pull request's author, resolves its threads with plain gh api graphql (resolveReviewThread). The two App-login variables, appauth.LoginEnv and api.legionAppLogins go with the bot rule.
specDepartures.spec: Spec v4, 'Stays': the reviewer's thread resolution through the daemon stays 'as it works today, less the Accepted: rule', and the pull request builds nothing for the open LEGION-656 thread question before it is answered.

specDepartures.evidence: Measured in round 1 from the planner's pod with its own App token: GET /user answers HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' to an installation token; the GraphQL viewer query answers legion-reviewer[bot]; packages/daemon/internal/api/real_github_test.go proves App identity with the same query.

acceptance: 1. An implementer and a subagent it launches each run `gh api graphql -f query='{viewer{login}}'` (GitHub refuses `GET /user` to an App installation token) and push a commit with plain `gh` and `git`, with no grant minted and no `legion gh` on the path; the push is attributed to the implement App. A reviewer session pushes its handoff as the review App.

specDepartures.plan: The identity proof is `gh api graphql -f query='{viewer{login}}'` (answers the App's bot login) instead of `gh api user`; the push and everything else in the line stand. Carried from the first plan; already built at this head.
specDepartures.spec: Acceptance 1: 'An implementer and a subagent it launches each run `gh api user` and push a commit with plain `gh` and `git`'.

workflowRecommendation: One implementer, tasks 0-13 in the plan's order: the Go server-side completion first (task 1) so the CLI deletions (task 2) compile against it, then threads by id, image drift, the contract paragraph, pi-legion, prompts, skills, docs, e2e, rigs, superseded lines; the four suite commands once at the end; then the PR body's Rollout paragraph. Stage 4a at the new head's image, then 4b and stage 3, are queued by the architect through the coordinator session; the implementer cannot run them from a pod.
